evidence.quote: Today’s decision to lower the federal funds rate target by ¼ percent, to 1.75 percent to 2 percent, is appropriate in light of the global developments I mentioned as well as muted inflation pressures.
And if the economy does turn down, then a more extensive sequence of rate cuts could be appropriate.
We are mindful that continued below-target inflation could lead to an unwelcome downward slide in longer-term inflation expectations.
So we do see those risks as actually more heightened now.
it is certainly possible that we will need to resume the organic growth of the balance sheet earlier than we thought.
The projections of appropriate policy show that participants generally anticipate only modest changes in the federal funds rate over the next couple of years.

parsed.rationale: The Fed cut rates as insurance against heightened downside risks from global growth and trade, with muted inflation, and left the door open to further cuts, while describing the baseline outlook as favorable and expecting only modest further adjustments. It also signaled possible earlier resumption of balance sheet growth.
